correctness.rationale: For all integers \(3\le p\le q\) and positive real \(t\), all exactly-two-leader pairs reduce by internal-vertex permutations to eight orbits. Constant-on-orbit and internal zero-sum invariant subspaces give eight explicit grounded inverse traces, with each zero-sum eigenvalue equal to its clique order. Six positive rational gap certificates discard six types; the remaining difference has sign \(p^2(q+2)-4(q-p)t\). At \(p=q\) it is positive; at \(p<q\) it changes sign exactly at \(t=p^2(q+2)/(4(q-p))\). Every equality and strict condition, optimal count, and objective follows. The standalone standard-library program was executed against the accompanying theorem and passed 5109 exact-rational direct matrix comparisons over 114 graph/weight cases and independent arithmetic-gap identity tests; enumeration is supporting evidence, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A canonical bottleneck graph with adjustable bridge conductance models coupled dense communities. The theorem provides the first complete all-size exact structural placement phase diagram for the examined literature: balanced communities always select two interior leaders, whereas unequal communities switch the larger community leader from interior to bridge gateway at an explicit size-dependent weight. Counts and exact minimum objective are determined throughout the continuous positive-weight domain, including equality. The sharp boundary quantifies when bridge strength overturns geographic dispersion and is not just a numerical or arbitrary finite invariant.
